_comment: Routing prompts for adr-author. should_not holds near misses: requests that sound like ADR work but belong to another skill, or to no skill at all.
should_trigger: Write an ADR for our decision to move session storage from cookies to Redis.
We've agreed billing only talks to the ledger through its API. Can you record that decision in docs/adr?
ADR 4 says we never call payments synchronously, but the code does now and that's fine. Supersede it.
Our architecture decision record about the event bus no longer matches the code. The code is right. Fix the record.
Record this architecture decision: all public endpoints go through the gateway in api/gateway.py.
Create a MADR for choosing Postgres full-text search over Elasticsearch, it's already decided.
Can you turn this decision into a proper decision record: services must not share database schemas.
Amend ADR 7: the rule about caching only applies to read endpoints, not writes.
Add a decision record explaining why we deliberately use raw SQL instead of an ORM in reports/.
Document the architecture decision we made yesterday to split notifications into its own service.
should_not: Does this README section sound like an AI wrote it? Tighten it up.
Should we use Kafka or SQS for the order events? Give me the trade-offs.
Grill me on my plan to split the monolith before I commit to it.
Convene a panel to review our build-vs-buy decision for the search service.
Review this diff for bugs before I merge it.
Implement the outbox pattern in events/outbox.py with tests.
Is this runbook easy to follow? Where do readers get lost?
Write the commit message for the staged changes.
Explain what an architecture decision record is and when teams use them.
Check whether our code still follows the decisions in docs/adr and list violations.
